title: Install on Kubernetes - Knowledge Check
description: Confirm you understand what dtwiz installs on a cluster, and why KSPM has to go on k3d.

questions.title: What does `dtwiz install kubernetes` deploy?
questions.content: You ran `dtwiz install kubernetes --yes`. What did it put on the cluster?

options.text: The Dynatrace Operator plus a DynaKube custom resource, which brings an ActiveGate, the OpenTelemetry collector and code injection
options.explanation: The operator is the controller; the DynaKube is what tells it what to monitor.

options.text: A OneAgent DaemonSet only, with no custom resources
options.explanation: That is the classic host-agent path. The Kubernetes flow is operator plus DynaKube.

options.text: Nothing on the cluster - it only writes local kubeconfig entries
options.explanation: It really does deploy workloads; that is why the wait can time out.

questions.explanation: install kubernetes = Dynatrace Operator + DynaKube (ActiveGate, OTel collector, code injection).
hints: Two things: the controller, and the custom resource that configures it.

questions.title: Why does the node-config-collector pod hang on k3d?
questions.content: After the install, one pod sits in `ContainerCreating` forever and dtwiz's wait times out. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: KSPM's node-config-collector needs real node host access, and k3d's "nodes" are containers rather than hosts
options.explanation: It mounts the host filesystem to run CIS/security benchmarks, which a container node cannot provide.

options.text: The operator failed to start, so none of its pods can schedule
options.explanation: The operator itself comes up fine - only that one DaemonSet is stuck.

options.text: The cluster has run out of memory
options.explanation: It is a host-access problem, not a capacity one; more memory changes nothing.

questions.explanation: KSPM (Kubernetes Security Posture Management) runs a DaemonSet that mounts the host filesystem. On k3d there is no real host to mount.
hints: Ask what the collector needs from the node, then ask what a k3d node actually is.

questions.title: What does `installDtwizKubernetes` do that the raw command does not?
questions.content: The lab gives you one helper instead of two commands. What does it add?

options.text: It runs `dtwiz install kubernetes --yes` and then `patchDynakubeDisableKspm`, so the cluster comes up k3d-clean in one call
options.explanation: Removing the kspm block makes the operator drop the DaemonSet that cannot run here.

options.text: It installs the operator without a DynaKube, so nothing needs patching
options.explanation: The DynaKube is still created - it is the kspm block inside it that is removed.

options.text: It disables the ActiveGate and the OpenTelemetry collector as well
options.explanation: Everything except KSPM stays fully functional.

questions.explanation: installDtwizKubernetes = install + patchDynakubeDisableKspm. Only KSPM is removed; operator, ActiveGate, OTel collector and code injection all stay.
hints: The tip box on the page spells out both halves.

learningObjectives: Know what dtwiz install kubernetes deploys.
Explain why KSPM cannot run on k3d.
Use installDtwizKubernetes to get a k3d-clean cluster.
